title: Professional and Therapy-Room Games
coreMove: Look at the helper and the helped together, because the professional role can be the cover that keeps the game respectable.
sourcePressure: Covers I'm Only Trying to Help You, Wooden Leg, Greenhouse, Stupid, and Psychiatry in helping-profession relationships, with care around disability and accountability.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Blaming clients, patients, employees, or students while treating the professional helper as outside the game.
sourceAlignmentTerms: I'm Only Trying to Help You

sourceAnchors.name: I'm Only Trying to Help You
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes a helper offering help that predictably fails, then using the failure as proof the recipient is hopeless and the helper blameless
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: I'm Only Trying to Help You can make failure useful to the helper because it proves the helper tried.

sourceAnchors.name: Wooden Leg
sourceAnchors.detail: the source distinguishes real limitation from deploying a limitation as permanent exemption from unrelated accountability
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The limitation may be real; the game begins when the limitation is used to cover a demand it does not actually touch.

sourceAnchors.name: Greenhouse
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes using psychological vocabulary to label feelings while avoiding direct experience and change
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Greenhouse keeps every feeling behind glass, labeled and watered, never lived.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: nonprofit case-management meeting with repeated unused referrals
exampleSpecs.audience: a social worker checking whether her rescue plan needs the client to fail
exampleSpecs.stakes: services, dignity, and the helper's self-image are all involved
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rebecca asks the client which referral he will actually use and what barrier blocked the last one, instead of adding a third impressive option.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I found another program that might help," Rebecca says, then hears the old script in her own voice.

exampleSpecs.domain: corporate coaching package for an executive who collects frameworks
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach recognizing Psychiatry-style vocabulary touring
exampleSpecs.stakes: expensive insight can replace one hard behavior change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matteo stops the terminology loop and asks the executive to make one phone call before the next session.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The leather notebook already has three models boxed in blue ink.

exampleSpecs.domain: university accessibility office reviewing missed lab work
exampleSpecs.audience: an adviser separating real accommodation from Wooden Leg deployment
exampleSpecs.stakes: respecting disability while keeping unrelated responsibilities clear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida grants the sensory accommodation and still requires the lab safety quiz by a new date.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The accessibility office window faces a courtyard full of construction noise.

exampleSpecs.domain: apprenticeship workshop where a trainee keeps acting helpless around measurements
exampleSpecs.audience: a mentor seeing Stupid as a lowered-expectations pattern
exampleSpecs.stakes: the trainee may lose skill and the mentor may enjoy being indispensable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben hands back the calipers and waits for the trainee to read the measurement out loud before stepping in.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can rescue a bad measurement so quickly that no one learns who needed the rescue.

exampleSpecs.domain: therapy group where emotion words replace actual contact
exampleSpecs.audience: a facilitator recognizing Greenhouse in polished self-observation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the group can admire insight while no risk is taken
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chiara asks the speaker to say the sentence directly to the person named, not about the feeling category.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What happens when every feeling has a label before anyone has felt it in the room?

exampleSpecs.domain: customer-success manager with a client who ignores onboarding then blames the tool
exampleSpecs.audience: a professional helper whose role invites endless rescue
exampleSpecs.stakes: renewal revenue can hide a repeated help-failure game
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf notices that each unused training session lets both sides keep their story, then moves to a written use criterion.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Two renewals later, Yusuf sees that the unused onboarding call was not an accident.

skillTargets: distinguish real limitation from Wooden Leg deployment

tryThisNowSpec: Before offering the next help, ask what would count as the other person using it. If no answer exists, the help may be part of the game.
